title: Business skills: which written processes do agents follow, and who controls them?
summary: Pass: Microsoft's documentation supports the availability controls, Dataverse update operations, sharing permissions and experience-based billing. The checklist asks readers to review sharing without a corresponding control row; that is a minor completeness issue.

claims.claim: Business skills are natural-language instructions describing organisational processes.
claims.quote: Business skills are natural-language instructions that capture how your organization gets work done.

claims.claim: Business skills are stored as Dataverse records.
claims.quote: Records of instructions, scripts, and resources that agents can discover and use to do things more accurately and efficiently.

claims.claim: A skill describes the steps for a particular type of work.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.claim: A skill describes the information required for that work.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.claim: A skill describes the business rules that apply.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.quote: They contain natural-language instructions that guide agent behavior, similar to how you might document a process for a new employee.

claims.quote: The agent retrieves the complete instructions and resources for a relevant skill.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Microsoft describes agent selection of skills as probabilistic.
claims.quote: Agent selection is probabilistic, so test representative requests before you share a skill broadly.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat can discover and use accessible active business skills through Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and connected agents can discover and use the skills you have access to and follow your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Copilot Cowork can discover and use accessible active business skills through Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and connected agents can discover and use the skills you have access to and follow your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Agents connected to Work IQ MCP can access business skills.
claims.quote: Both MCP servers can provide access to business skills, but they serve different integration patterns.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP can discover business applications paths across environments available to the user.
claims.quote: Can discover business applications paths across environments available to the user. Name the intended environment when the user has access to several.

claims.claim: Agents connected directly to Dataverse MCP can use skills without Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: Business skills also remain supported in agents connected directly to the Dataverse MCP server, without connecting through Work IQ MCP.

claims.claim: A direct Dataverse MCP connection targets one environment.
claims.quote: The MCP connection is configured for a specific Dataverse environment.

claims.claim: The Power Apps maker navigation to business skills is More > Business skills.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps and select your environment. In the left navigation pane, select More, and then select Business skills.

claims.claim: Makers can write skills manually.
claims.quote: You can also write the skill yourself in the same editor without using Skill Builder.

claims.claim: Skill Builder is an agent that helps create business skills.
claims.quote: Skill Builder is a specialized agent that helps you create business skills through natural-language conversation.

claims.claim: Makers can upload Skill.md or .zip files.
claims.quote: If you already have a skill in a Skill.md (markdown) or .zip file, upload it instead of creating the content from scratch.

claims.claim: Copilot or agents connected to Work IQ or Dataverse MCP can create business skills.
claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server:

claims.claim: Copilot or agents connected to Work IQ or Dataverse MCP can update business skills.
claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server:

claims.claim: The Dataverse MCP upsert_skill tool creates skills.
claims.quote: upsert_skill | Creates a new business skill or updates an existing one.

claims.claim: The Dataverse MCP delete_skill tool deletes skills.
claims.quote: delete_skill | Deletes an existing business skill from the environment.

claims.claim: A skill can have only one active version.
claims.quote: A skill can have only one active version.

claims.claim: Save retains a working copy without changing the version agents use.
claims.quote: Saves your working copy without changing the version agents use. A new skill remains inactive. If the skill already has an active version, that version stays active.

claims.where: What it is: versioning; Why it matters
claims.claim: Save and activate makes the saved changes the active version for agents.
claims.quote: Makes your changes the active version, including its associated resources. The previous active version remains in version history.

claims.where: What it is: versioning; Governance controls: Watching
claims.claim: Version history records who changed or activated a version.
claims.quote: It identifies the active version, shows saved changes that aren't active, and records who changed or activated a version and when.

claims.claim: Business skills are solution-aware.
claims.quote: Business skills are solution-aware, which means you can package them into solutions for application lifecycle management (ALM).

claims.claim: Solution exports include only a skill's active version.
claims.quote: Managed and unmanaged solution exports include only the active version of each skill, along with its metadata and associated resources.

claims.claim: Skills are user-owned records in the Business Skill (skill) table.
claims.quote: Business Skill (Skill) table/entity reference (Microsoft Dataverse); OwnershipType | UserOwned

claims.claim: General access can make a skill available to everyone in the environment.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: General access provides view-only permission.
claims.quote: For general access, choose Anyone can view to allow everyone in the organization to use this skill. This option provides view-only access.

claims.claim: Owners can share skills through selected Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: Owners can provide general access to everyone in the environment, share with selected Dataverse security roles, or provide direct access to specific users or groups.

claims.claim: Owners can grant direct access to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Owners can provide general access to everyone in the environment, share with selected Dataverse security roles, or provide direct access to specific users or groups.

claims.claim: Security-role access can grant view or edit permission.
claims.quote: Security role access and direct access can provide view or edit permissions.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview lists Dataverse business skills as preview.
claims.quote: Business skills with Dataverse intelligence (preview) are natural-language instructions that encode your organization's processes, policies, and domain knowledge in a format agents can interpret and execute.

claims.where: What it is: wider skills terminology
claims.claim: Work IQ uses skills as a wider category of task-specific instructions.
claims.quote: Skills provide task-specific instructions that help Copilot and agents complete specialized work with higher speed and precision.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: How the controls stack
claims.claim: The environment Work IQ setting enables business skills.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: How the controls stack; What to check
claims.claim: Turning Work IQ off makes business skills unavailable in the environment.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Nonproduction environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft deferred the plan to enable Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.claim: Manage feature settings lists the Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) setting with a default of Off.
claims.quote: Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences | When On, allows reusable business context business skills to be used by your agents. | Off

claims.claim: The business skills overview and create pages name no licence specific to skills.
claims.quote: Searched: "business skills" "licensing" Dataverse. Read business-skill-overview, business-skills prerequisites, Sales agent prerequisites and Work IQ API licensing; the general skill pages name no skill-specific licence.

claims.claim: Creating skills requires a Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled.
claims.quote: A Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled by a Power Platform administrator.

claims.claim: Creating skills requires permissions allowing creation in the environment.
claims.quote: Permissions to create or use business skills in the environment.

claims.claim: Using skills through Business Applications in Work IQ requires access to a supported Copilot experience or agent.
claims.quote: To use skills through Business Applications in Work IQ, you need access to a supported Copilot experience or connected agent.

claims.claim: The create page points to Work IQ API licensing requirements.
claims.quote: For Work IQ licensing requirements, see Licensing requirements.

claims.claim: Work IQ API uses usage-based licensing.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is paid for with Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ cost is tracked by consuming experience rather than a dedicated business applications category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting Cowork tasks is attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.claim: Coding agents and custom integrations calling Work IQ directly report that consumption under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The applicable Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat entitlement includes business-data grounding.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.

claims.claim: Spending policies set consumption limits for the consuming experience.
claims.quote: Spending policies let you choose the users and services covered, set a shared monthly limit, add a per-user limit, and receive alerts as consumption approaches a threshold.

claims.claim: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.

claims.claim: The cost of a skill-following request varies with the work performed.
claims.quote: Complexity, the context needed, and the work performed affect consumption.

claims.claim: A credit rate specific to business skills is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "business skills" "credit" "rate"; "business skills" "Copilot Credits" "billing" rate. Read Work IQ understand-costs and API licensing; inspected Copilot Studio billing-rate search excerpts. No skill-specific rate appeared.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Two-role trap; Governance controls
claims.claim: Security-role sharing requires both the selected role and Skill Sharing Role; either alone is insufficient.
claims.quote: Only users who have both Customer Service Representative and Skill Sharing Role can access it. Having either role by itself isn't enough.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Participation is not access control
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Participation is not access control
claims.claim: App Access manages agentic application access to environment data.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Studio reads little of a resource
claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents support only text-based skill resource files.
claims.quote: When using business skills with an agent in Microsoft Copilot Studio, only text-based resource files are supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Studio reads little of a resource
claims.claim: A Copilot Studio agent reads only the first 20 KB of a text-based skill resource file.
claims.quote: The agent can only read the first 20 KB of data from a text-based resource file.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Studio reads little of a resource
claims.claim: Skill resource attachments have a 20 MB limit.
claims.quote: In Resources, select Add Files to attach reference materials that agents need when following the skill, such as policy documents, standard operating procedures, templates, forms, or calculations (20 MB limit).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Studio reads little of a resource
claims.claim: Skill file uploads have a 30 MB limit.
claims.quote: Upload your skill file (30 MB limit).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deletion is permanent
claims.claim: Deleting a skill is permanent and cannot be undone.
claims.quote: Deleting a skill is permanent and can't be undone.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deletion is permanent
claims.claim: Agents referencing a deleted skill can no longer use it.
claims.quote: Any agents that reference the deleted skill can no longer use it.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Deletion is permanent
claims.claim: Deactivation preserves skill content and version history.
claims.quote: Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No usage view; Governance controls: Watching
claims.claim: The Business skills page does not show per-skill runtime usage.
claims.quote: The Business skills page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is unavailable in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ reaches the environment switch.
claims.quote: Select Manage. Select the environment that you want to manage. On the command bar, select Settings. Select Product > Features. Find Work IQ, and then turn the setting on or off.

claims.claim: Managing the Work IQ environment switch requires an environment administrator account.
claims.quote: You need an environment administrator account.

claims.claim: The Work IQ environment setting also enables semantic modelling.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder.

claims.claim: No API, PowerShell or CLI operation for the environment Work IQ switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment setting Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell enable disable intelligence; Dataverse organization "Work IQ" enable API setting. Read defaults, participation and pac admin excerpts; no deciding operation found.

claims.claim: Power Apps > More > Business skills > skill > Deactivate stops discovery and use of the active skill.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select More, and then select Business skills. To stop agents from discovering or using an active skill: Select a skill, and then select Deactivate from the command bar or the three-dot menu.

claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/skills(<skillid>) can update the skill state through statecode.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/skills; Primary key: skillid; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; statecode | Edm.Int32 | Status of the Business Skill

claims.claim: Skill statecode values are 0 for Active and 1 for Inactive.
claims.quote: statecode | Edm.Int32 | Status of the Business Skill; 0 | Active; 1 | Inactive

claims.claim: The Copilot audience control is at Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: The audience choices are No users, All users and Specific groups.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default. To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: How the controls stack
claims.claim: The audience setting governs the Microsoft 365 Copilot route, not direct Dataverse MCP access.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 admin center provides a setting that determines who can access business applications through Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: No automation for the Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot audience setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta Work IQ MCP block tools Copilot business applications audience settings API; "Business Applications data" "Copilot" Graph settings API. Read defaults and manage-ai-experience-access; results documented UI, not audience-update automation.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block blocks the Work IQ MCP server.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center. Select Agents > Tools. Select Work IQ MCP. Review its current availability. To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: How the controls stack
claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP availability control applies to the entire server for connected AI experiences and coding agents.
claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP server has its own availability control for connected AI experiences and coding agents. This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: AI Administrator manages the Microsoft 365 admin center connection settings.
claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: No automation for the Work IQ MCP server's availability block is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "Graph" "block" MCP admin API; "Work IQ MCP" "Graph" "availability" API admin. Read manage-ai-experience-access and Work IQ API/tool reference excerpts; no server-availability update operation found.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance controls: How the controls stack; What to check
claims.claim: The direct Dataverse MCP client control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled.
claims.quote: Select Manage > Environments. Select the Environment Name ... Settings ... Product > Features ... Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Select Advanced Settings ... Open the client record you want ... set Is Enabled to Yes.

claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients(<allowedmcpclientid>) updates client enablement through isenabled.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients; Primary key: allowedmcpclientid; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator manages environment settings and allowed Dataverse MCP clients.
claims.quote: Power Platform administrator role in order to access Dataverse MCP server environment settings, enable allowed MCP clients, create or edit an environment group, and change connector policies.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance controls: How the controls stack
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot Studio Dataverse MCP client is enabled in all environments by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Copilot Studio client for Dataverse MCP is enabled for all environments.

claims.where: Governance controls: Roles; Why it matters
claims.claim: Basic User can create skills they own.
claims.quote: Basic User | Can create skills that they own. Environment Maker | Can create and share skills that they own. System Administrator or System Customizer | Can create and share skills.

claims.claim: Admins can share a skill with any security role.
claims.quote: You can share a skill with roles assigned to you. Admins can share with any role.

claims.where: What to check: list active skills, owners and access
claims.claim: Every control the checklist asks readers to review appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: "list the active skills, their owners and who has access". Table: availability, activation, Copilot audience, Work IQ MCP blocking and allowed Dataverse MCP clients; no skill-sharing row.
claims.fix: Narrow the checklist bullet to: 'Open Business skills in Power Apps for each Work IQ environment and list the active skills.'

claims.claim: Each skill has an owner who controls access.
claims.quote: Each skill has an owner who controls access.

claims.where: Governance controls: No admin-centre sharing switch
claims.claim: No admin-centre switch restricting business-skill sharing is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "business skills" "sharing" "admin center" restrict. Read overview, create/share instructions, Work IQ administration and managed-environment-sharing-limits. The latter covers apps, flows and agents, not Dataverse skill records.

claims.where: Governance controls: No admin-centre sharing switch
claims.claim: An owner shares a skill by selecting it on the Business skills page and selecting Share.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select More, and then select Business skills. Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu.

claims.where: Governance controls: No admin-centre sharing switch
claims.claim: An administrator must assign Skill Sharing Role for users to access skills through security-role sharing.
claims.quote: Security role access requires users to have two roles. An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls stack
claims.claim: For Sales agent, the documented control changes apply to new agent interactions.
claims.quote: Changes apply to new agent interactions.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls stack
claims.claim: Sales agent users might need to refresh an existing session after these changes.
claims.quote: Users might need to refresh an existing session.

claims.claim: Which audit events identify an agent retrieving and following a Dataverse skill remains an open question.
claims.quote: Searched: "business skills" audit events retrieval. Read skill troubleshooting and Work IQ overview. Work IQ says tool invocations are logged, but no returned passage identifies a skill-retrieval or skill-following audit event.

claims.claim: System Administrator can create and share business skills.
claims.quote: System Administrator or System Customizer | Can create and share skills.

claims.claim: System Customizer can create and share business skills.
claims.quote: System Administrator or System Customizer | Can create and share skills.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Environment Maker can create and share skills they own.
claims.quote: Environment Maker | Can create and share skills that they own.

claims.claim: Other skill owners can share with security roles assigned to them.
claims.quote: You can share a skill with roles assigned to you. Admins can share with any role.

claims.claim: All users is the default Copilot audience option.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default.

claims.claim: Direct access can grant view or edit permission.
claims.quote: Security role access and direct access can provide view or edit permissions.

claims.claim: The Dataverse MCP upsert_skill tool updates existing skills.
claims.quote: upsert_skill | Creates a new business skill or updates an existing one.

claims.claim: The Work IQ environment setting enables access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder.

claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder.
